English Definition: all the time, or often
Example Sentence: The software on my computer is constantly asking for updates, which is annoying.
Example 2: He is constantly complaining about the weather, but he never moves to a sunnier place.
Example 3: The market is changing constantly, so we must adapt our strategy every week.

English Definition: clearly noticeable, easy to identify
Example Sentence: There is a distinct smell of burning wood in the air
Example 2: The two species of birds are distinct, even though they look somewhat similar.
Example 3: I got the distinct impression that she was lying to me during the interview.

English Definition: inactive, but which could become active in the future
Example Sentence: The volcano has been dormant for 500 years, but scientists believe it could erupt again.
Example 2: Bears remain dormant in their dens during the long winter months.
Example 3: The virus can lie dormant in the body for years before symptoms appear.

English Definition: boring, without bright color
Example Sentence: The office walls were painted a drab gray, making the room feel depressing.
Example 2: She grew tired of her drab uniform and longed to wear colorful dresses again.
Example 3: His presentation was quite drab and failed to capture the audience's attention.

English Definition: full of action and excitement or sudden and striking
Example Sentence: There has been a dramatic increase in sales since we launched the new website.
Example 2: She made a dramatic entrance at the party, wearing a bright red gown.
Example 3: Don't be so dramatic

English Definition: containing a lot of detail OR to explain further
Example Sentence: The ceiling of the palace was decorated with elaborate carvings and gold leaf.
Example 2: He prepared an elaborate dinner with five different courses for his guests.
Example 3: Could you please elaborate on your idea? I don't fully understand it yet.

English Definition: basic
Example Sentence: My knowledge of coding is very elementary
Example 2: Sherlock Holmes often said the solution was elementary, but Watson was always confused.
Example 3: They made an elementary mistake in the calculation that ruined the whole experiment.

English Definition: in a way that is not regular, certain or expected
Example Sentence: The stock market has been erratic lately, causing investors to panic.
Example 2: His breathing became erratic after running the marathon.
Example 3: Because of her erratic work schedule, it is hard to plan meetings with her.

English Definition: real, honest, sincere
Example Sentence: This purse is made of genuine leather, not plastic.
Example 2: She showed genuine concern for the homeless people in her community.
Example 3: I think he is a genuine person

English Definition: huge, very big
Example Sentence: Cleaning up the ocean is a mammoth task that requires international cooperation.
Example 2: The construction company built a mammoth shopping mall in the center of the city.
Example 3: The mammoth corporation bought out all its smaller competitors.

English Definition: telling other people what to do in an excessively authoritarian manner
Example Sentence: I moved out because I couldn't handle my overbearing father anymore.
Example 2: Her boss has an overbearing management style that makes everyone nervous.
Example 3: The heat in the desert can be overbearing during the middle of the day.

English Definition: main, most important or best quality
Example Sentence: The prime minister will give a speech tonight regarding the economy.
Example 2: The police consider him the prime suspect in the robbery case.
Example 3: This restaurant serves prime cuts of steak that are incredibly tender.

English Definition: basic
Example Sentence: The tribe only had rudimentary tools made of stone and wood.
Example 2: He has only a rudimentary grasp of French, so he struggles to order food.
Example 3: The shelter provided was rudimentary, offering only a roof and a dirt floor.

English Definition: to obtain something from something else
Example Sentence: Many modern medicines are derived from rare plants found in the rainforest.
Example 2: He derives a lot of pleasure from painting landscapes on the weekend.
Example 3: The word 'democracy' derives from the Greek language.

English Definition: to spread over a large area
Example Sentence: The seeds of this flower are light enough for the wind to disperse them.
Example 2: The fog began to disperse as soon as the sun came up.
Example 3: Police used tear gas to disperse the violent protesters.

English Definition: to remove or take away
Example Sentence: The doctor told him to eliminate sugar from his diet to improve his health.
Example 2: Our team was eliminated from the tournament in the semi-finals.
Example 3: New technology creates jobs, but it can also eliminate old ones.

English Definition: to surround, make a circle around something
Example Sentence: Tall medieval walls encircle the old town, protecting its history.
Example 2: The enemy troops tried to encircle the base and cut off supplies.
Example 3: A beautiful gold chain encircled her neck.

English Definition: to make something exist (feeling or situation)
Example Sentence: His rude comments engendered a lot of anger among the staff.
Example 2: Confidence in the leader can engender loyalty in the team.
Example 3: Poverty can often engender crime in neglected neighborhoods.

English Definition: to be so interesting as to absorb someone completely
Example Sentence: She was so engrossed in her book that she missed her train stop.
Example 2: The video game is designed to engross players for hours at a time.
Example 3: The lecture was fascinating and engrossed the entire audience.

English Definition: to succeed in doing something OR to control
Example Sentence: I don't know how you manage to work full-time and raise three kids.
Example 2: He was hired to manage the finance department of the company.
Example 3: Can you manage this heavy box on your own, or do you need help?

English Definition: to make someone very embarrassed
Example Sentence: She was mortified when she realized she had her shirt on inside out.
Example 2: It would mortify me to have to sing in front of a large crowd.
Example 3: His parents were mortified by his bad behavior at the wedding.

English Definition: to get something
Example Sentence: You need to obtain a permit from the city before you can build a garage.
Example 2: Police are trying to obtain surveillance footage from the store.
Example 3: It is difficult to obtain fresh vegetables in this remote area.

English Definition: to refuse to accept, believe or use
Example Sentence: The bank had to reject his loan application due to his poor credit score.
Example 2: Her body began to reject the kidney transplant shortly after the surgery.
Example 3: He rejected the idea that money brings happiness.

English Definition: to be a good reason for
Example Sentence: How can you justify spending so much money on a car?
Example 2: The end does not always justify the means.
Example 3: He tried to justify his lateness by blaming the traffic.

English Definition: an award or privilege granted for a person's good actions
Example Sentence: The restaurant received the highest accolade: three Michelin stars.
Example 2: She has won many accolades for her acting, including an Oscar.
Example 3: Despite the critical accolades, the movie did not make much money.

English Definition: a place or feature designed to make life more pleasant
Example Sentence: The hotel offers many amenities, including a pool, a gym, and free Wi-Fi.
Example 2: The apartment is small, but it is close to local amenities like shops and parks.
Example 3: Running water is a basic amenity that everyone should have access to.

English Definition: a fault, mistake or weakness
Example Sentence: There is a major flaw in your logic that makes the whole argument invalid.
Example 2: This diamond is expensive because it does not have a single visible flaw.
Example 3: His jealousy is a character flaw that ruined his marriage.

English Definition: the cutting, picking or collecting crops
Example Sentence: The farmers are working late because the wheat harvest has begun.
Example 2: It was a bad year for the grape harvest due to the heavy rains.
Example 3: We must harvest the apples before the first frost arrives.

English Definition: a person who is much admired and respected
Example Sentence: Elvis Presley was a massive idol for teenagers in the 1950s.
Example 2: As a young footballer, his idol was always Lionel Messi.
Example 3: The ancient temple contained a gold idol that people worshipped.

English Definition: an extremely small amount of something
Example Sentence: Physics studies how subatomic particles interact with each other.
Example 2: There isn't a single particle of truth in the rumors spreading about him.
Example 3: Dust particles in the air can trigger asthma attacks.
